subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should core permanently adopt this dedicated opt-in timeout plus synchronous queue fence as the contract for abandoning non-cooperative deferred context-engine maintenance?
rationale: Source review can establish that the implementation is internally coherent, but it cannot decide whether OpenClaw should add another config knob, expose a generic queue callback, or define plugin maintenance as abandonable without cooperative cancellation.

options.title: Sponsor the opt-in contract
options.body: Approve the dedicated disabled-by-default setting and synchronous queue fence, then rebase and validate the exact merged head.

options.title: Unify with compaction cancellation
options.body: Require the timeout to reuse an existing host safety budget and a context-engine-owned cooperative cancellation contract instead of adding parallel policy.

options.title: Defer the core contract
options.body: Close or pause the PR until maintainers are ready to define bounded background-maintenance semantics across plugins.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Approve the dedicated disabled-by-default setting and synchronous queue fence, then rebase and validate the exact merged head.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent context-engine and compaction lifecycle work makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the timeout and plugin-abandonment policy.
